To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) consistent inference of population growth is not possible for a sample size n, even in the idealized setting of this paper, and 2) maximum likelihood estimators of the parameters describing population growth are not asymptotically normal, even in the setting of this paper.
the maximum likelihood estimators of population growth rates, mutation rates, and the number of historical mutations, converge in probability to the true parameter values.

(i) population growth rate cannot be consistently estimated from genealogies; (ii) the maximum likelihood estimator of the growth rate is asymptotically normal with a nonstandard variance; and (iii) the growth rate can be consistently estimated from DNA sequences if a sufficiently large number of loci are used, provided the mutation rate is known.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fundamental question of whether the population history of a group of individuals can be inferred from a single DNA sequence.
how much information about population history can be extracted from DNA sequence data.
the question of whether it is possible to estimate the parameters of a population history model from DNA sequence data, given a sample size of interest.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in this idealised world, population history cannot be inferred accurately from DNA sequence data.
, in the absence of recombination, population history cannot be accurately inferred from DNA data.
, for a sample of DNA sequences, the population history cannot be estimated consistently.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
population history is very difficult to estimate accurately from single locus DNA sequence data, even if the tree relating the data is known.
, although population history can be estimated from DNA data, the information content in DNA data about the population history is very limited.
the coalescent process provides a lower limit to the difficulty of inferring population history from sequence data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
population history cannot be accurately inferred from a single locus DNA sample.
the amount of information about population history in DNA sequence data is limited.
